answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can root trust in a collateralized vouching web: each endorsement is bonded, so an established agent stakes reputation when vouching for a newcomer and is slashed if that identity later cheats. Trust spreads like pigment through the social graph, each node tinted by the risk of everyone who backed it. A fake swarm cannot reach the zenith of influence, since its only vouchers are other fakes nobody will stake on. Like a juniper from one hardy rootstock, credible identity grafts one bonded relationship at a time, making mass identity farming pointless.
